taskDescription: Drag each word into the correct blank to complete the comparison of the two forms of severe protein–energy malnutrition.
textField: In *marasmus* the child loses subcutaneous fat and muscle, giving an 'old-man' face, while in *kwashiorkor* pitting *oedema* masks the wasting and gives a 'moon face'. The liver normally exports triglyceride in *VLDL* particles.

overallFeedback.feedback: Marasmus reflects total energy-and-protein deficit with gross wasting, while kwashiorkor reflects disproportionate protein deficit with oedema from low albumin. Kwashiorkor commonly includes fatty liver, but its pathogenesis is multifactorial; reduced apolipoprotein synthesis limiting VLDL export is the traditional explanation, but it is not an established universal mechanism — the presence or absence of oedema remains the single feature that separates the two on clinical examination.
